title: observability: token-level tracing + metric aggregation + alert tuning
author: Priya Nair
description: Adds token-level tracing hooks across the serving runtime, aggregated metrics for token-cost and token-latency breakdowns, and tuned alert rules to reduce noisy pagers. This PR implements: 1) a lightweight tracing span emitted per token-generation step (configurable sampling), 2) a new aggregation pipeline that rolls up token-level latencies and cost by route/model/region for 1h/24h windows, 3) updated Grafana dashboards with token-cost vs latency heatmaps and per-route percentiles, 4) alert rule changes to focus on P95 token latency and token-cost-per-1k predictions instead of noisy per-request thresholds, and 5) integration tests and a migration guide. Motivation: customer incidents and internal audits showed we lacked visibility into token-level performance regressions and cost spikes; existing alerts generated high noise. This change reduces noise, improves signal for model regressions, and enables cost-attribution by route and model. Backwards compatibility: hooks are opt-in via cluster config and default sampling is 1/1000 to control overhead. See linked Linear tasks ENG-4572 (token tracing pipeline) and ENG-4610 (alert tuning).
